meta.note: Dev set used ONLY to calibrate abstention thresholds.

questions.question: How long may personal data be kept in a form that permits identification of data subjects?
questions.expected_answer: No longer than necessary for the purposes of processing (Art. 5(1)(e)).

questions.question: On which grounds does a data subject have the right to obtain erasure of personal data?
questions.expected_answer: Art. 17(1): no longer necessary, consent withdrawn, objection, unlawful processing, legal obligation, child's data.

expected_evidence.snippet: right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data

questions.question: What may a processor not do without prior authorisation of the controller?
questions.expected_answer: Engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation (Art. 28(2)).

expected_evidence.snippet: shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation

questions.question: Which traffic data may be processed for subscriber billing under the ePrivacy Directive?
questions.expected_answer: Traffic data necessary for subscriber billing and interconnection payments (Art. 6(2)).

expected_evidence.snippet: traffic data necessary for the purposes of subscriber billing

questions.question: What must data holders do when data cannot be directly accessed by the user from the connected product?
questions.expected_answer: Make the readily available data available to the user without undue delay (Data Act Art. 4(1)).

expected_evidence.snippet: where data cannot be directly accessed by the user from the connected product

questions.question: On what basis may a transfer of personal data to a third country take place without further authorisation?
questions.expected_answer: Where the Commission has decided that the third country ensures an adequate level of protection (Art. 45(1)).

expected_evidence.snippet: a transfer of personal data to a third country or an international organisation may take place where the commission has decided

questions.question: Which principles must personal data processing follow, and what must the controller be able to demonstrate about them?
questions.expected_answer: Art. 5(1) lists the principles; Art. 5(2): the controller is responsible for and must be able to demonstrate compliance (accountability).

expected_evidence.snippet: able to demonstrate compliance with, paragraph 1

questions.question: What must a controller check before using a processor, and what must the contract with the processor provide?
questions.expected_answer: Use only processors providing sufficient guarantees (Art. 28(1)); processing is governed by a binding contract (Art. 28(3)).

expected_evidence.snippet: processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract
